media:group.media:title: Mobilizing for Election Day
media:group.media:description:
Dozens came together joining Hopkins Votes to recognize Election Day. The group gathered for HOP to the Polls at the Beach on the Homewood campus, helping people register to vote, providing info about polling locations, and offering pizza to mark the day. The group then walked together to the Enoch Pratt Free Library-Waverly Branch polling location, giving students, faculty, and staff the chance to make their voice heard.
Video by: Aubrey Morse

entry.title: Demons, Witches, and Vampires at the Historical Collection - Lunch with the Libraries & Museums

media:group.media:title: Demons, Witches, and Vampires at the Historical Collection - Lunch with the Libraries & Museums
media:group.media:description:
Presented by Hopkins at Home, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, the Institute of the History of Medicine, and the Welch Medical Library
Join Curator Michael Seminara in the Rare Book Room at the Institute of the History of Medicine for a look at some of the Historical Collection’s most terrifying books! We’ll discuss connections between medicine and the occult from the 16th century to the mid-19th century. We’ll see exorcism manuals, conflicting theories on witchcraft, a grimoire, and accounts of vampiric activity. The live virtual Q&A with Michael will be moderated by Donna Hesson.
For more information about the books shown in this video, please use the library's catalog links below: • Manuale exorcistarum https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991002687669707861 • Alexicacon, hoc est opus de maleficiis, ac morbis maleficis https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991002687699707861 • Flagellvm daemonvm https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991007038609707861 •Compendio dell'arte essorcistica https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991003489739707861 • De praestigiis daemonum https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991001606909707861 • The wonders of the invisible world https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991011372689707861 • Traité sur les apparitions des esprits, et sur les vampires https://catalyst.library.jhu.edu/permalink/01JHU_INST/b9593h/alma991060976641907861

entry.title: What Can Elite Sports Can Teach Us About the Future of Health?

media:group.media:title: What Can Elite Sports Can Teach Us About the Future of Health?
media:group.media:description: High-level sports is a laboratory for health data: biomechanical sensing, individualized recovery, injury prevention, rehabilitation, nutrition, mental performance, and more. Which insights and breakthroughs from this increasingly tech-enhanced world will trickle down to everyone else — and how will that make us stronger, healthier, and more durable? Fast Company and the Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg Center invited Olympians, tech leaders, and health experts to explore the technologies and strategies helping athletes perform.

media:group.media:title: Midterms: The state of collective leadership
media:group.media:description: Scott Warren, professor of practice at the SNF Agora Institute at Johns Hopkins University, breaks down the key factors encouraging dysfunction over collaboration between political parties and what can be done to re-establish a system that rewards bipartisanship and strengthens institutional trust.

entry.title: Johns Hopkins Alumni Association Awards Series: Pioneers of Innovation

media:group.media:title: Johns Hopkins Alumni Association Awards Series: Pioneers of Innovation
media:group.media:description:
• Celebrating Johns Hopkins' Sesquicentennial; presented by Hopkins at Home and the Johns Hopkins University Alumni Association • Featuring Shelly Blake-Plock (Ed '05), Kenneth Harris (WSE '17), David Heyman (SAIS '96), and Nicole Gaudelli (A&S '13); moderated by Robert Lord (SOM '22)
What does it take to turn a bold idea into meaningful change? How do innovators navigate uncertainty, challenge conventional thinking, and transform possibility into progress?
Join us for an inspiring conversation with four Johns Hopkins alumni whose pioneering work is shaping the future across education, aerospace, national security, biotechnology, and beyond. Drawing from careers at the forefront of discovery and innovation, these leaders explore the curiosity, creativity, and persistence required to pursue ambitious ideas—and the experiences that have shaped their approach to solving complex problems.
From developing new technologies for learning and contributing to groundbreaking space exploration to strengthening national security and advancing gene-editing therapies for genetic disease, our panelists demonstrate the many forms innovation can take. They reflect on pivotal moments in their careers, the risks and challenges inherent in doing something new, and how their Johns Hopkins experiences helped prepare them to push boundaries and imagine what comes next.
Featured panelists include:
Shelly Blake-Plock (Ed '05), CEO of Yet Analytics, driving innovation in educational technology and data science for learning advancement; Emeritus JH Leadership Fellow (Cohort 3) Kenneth Harris (WSE '17), aerospace engineer featured by Forbes, contributing to high-profile missions including the James Webb Space Telescope David Heyman (SAIS '96), nationally recognized thought leader in innovation, risk management, and national security and the founder of three technology companies Nicole Gaudelli (A&S '13), Entrepreneur in Residence at GV (Google Ventures) and inventor of the adenine base editor (ABE), a groundbreaking gene-editing technology with the potential to transform treatments for sickle cell disease and other genetic disorders.
Our conversation is moderated by Robert Lord (SOM '22), Senior Vice President of Data & Digital Research & Development at Vizient, Emeritus JH Leadership Fellow (Cohort 2).

entry.title: Lunch with the Libraries & Museums - Artists’ Books from A to B and Back Again

media:group.media:title: Lunch with the Libraries & Museums - Artists’ Books from A to B and Back Again
media:group.media:description:
Presented in partnership with Lifelong Learning and Hopkins at Home, Lunch with the Libraries & Museums is a series of free, online, public lectures through which staff from the Sheridan Libraries & University Museums discuss ongoing research, teaching, and curatorial work.
What do a miniature mannequin dummy, a 30-year-old noodle, and a bound set of keys have in common? They’re all artist books, imaginative works that push the boundaries of traditional bookmaking and challenge how we define books, storytelling, and reading itself.
Join Special Collections Outreach Librarian Heidi Herr to explore the fascinating genre of book arts, discover highlights from the Sheridan Libraries collections, and get a sneak peek at our recently acquired archive of renowned book artist Maureen Cummins.

entry.title: Full Event: How AI is Transforming Medicine | Next Conversations

media:group.media:title: Full Event: How AI is Transforming Medicine | Next Conversations
media:group.media:description:
See the full event here. Moderated by NPR’s, Steve Inskeep, Johns Hopkins University’s Ashani Weeraratna & Vasan Yegnasubramanian join the stage with, Pulitzer Prize-winning author, Siddhartha Mukherjee In this thought-provoking conversation about how artificial intelligence is reshaping the future of medicine, biology, and cancer research. From early cancer detection through blood-based screening to the rise of generative chemistry and, possibly a new discipline of science, this discussion highlights how AI is accelerating discoveries once thought impossible.
At the same time, the conversation raises an essential question: as technology advances, how do we preserve the human side of healthcare—clinical judgment, trust, and the doctor-patient relationship? With breakthroughs emerging alongside concerns about safety, funding, and responsible innovation, this dialogue offers a compelling look at both the promise and the challenge of a new era in biology.
#johnshopkins #jhu150 #nextconversations
